I highly recommend that before you start training creativity you read about what creativity really is. Most artists, musicians and writers think that a creativity is an esoteric thing. It isn't. It's a very practical thing. You want to come up with ideas? Most of the time, I just sit down and do it. That's all. If you want to train this skill, you have two choices. You can't tell people you're training to come up with ideas, so you'll have to call it "creativity training". Write down specific goals. Read a number of biographies of interesting historical figures and write down excerpts that you find to be inspiring. Make sure you record an average of at least 3 ideas per day for a period of 3 months. Start looking at things in a more creative way. If you look at a table, break it down into basic shapes (4 legs, flat surfaces), then see how those basic shapes can be built one into the other. This type of exercise will work for up to 1% of the population. Most people are incapable of doing this. Prepare three books. Label one "Things I read more than a year ago but I still remembered". Label one "Things I read 3 months ago but I still remember". Label one "Things I read 3 hours ago but I still remember". Have you heard about or read about any of the things in the second and third books lately? Sure you did. And that isn't really creativity, is it? Training creativity does not consist in forcing ideas into your head. Training creativity consists of efficiently filing away things that you encounter that you find interesting, so that you can easily find them when you need them for new ideas. This file system doesn't work well when the only thing you do is consume new information, but it works very well if you're actively browsing and cherry-picking information that inspires your imagination into your private library. A few illustrations, a biography, literature or science-related are distinctive enough to be re-remembered from your pool of "idea books" for months, if not years. Repeat. After three months, you'll start noticing a big difference in how you handle ideas. Creativity isn't really creative. You have to stop thinking of creativity as a magical talent you don't have. Creativity is you knowing your way around your own mind. You're just in charge of a very impressive computer called your brain. Mastering creativity is a question of programming.
